evidence: arXiv:2607.17957 (Yang, Lu, Liu, Kang, Zhang, Bansal, Rajmohan, Ma; 20 Jul 2026). Abstract: 'no failing test localizes where the consumer breaks'. Table V 'Impact of evidence form on pass rate': raw upstream evidence -7.4 to -23.2 pp vs no-evidence baseline.
correction: Location: Sec. IV-A is 'Problem Formulation' and does not compare raw vs structured evidence; cite Abstract + Table V (raw evidence vs no-evidence 'Minimal' baseline) for the 7-23 pp figure.

evidence: arXiv:2605.28148 (Pujara, Zhu, Chen; 27 May 2026). Abstract: 'DeltaMCP enables developers to only update the affected tooling of MCP servers' given a new OpenAPI spec release; evaluated on Azure REST API specs.

arXiv:2607.14642 (Liu et al., 16 Jul 2026). Abstract quote matches (13.7%, 14.4%). Sec 5.2 'MCP Server Evolution': 11 operators at TOOL/PARAM/DESC levels incl. tool deletion/replacement; paper never says 'interface-level'; backward compatibility mentioned only for mutation process generally.
correction: Frontier agents (GPT-5.4, Claude-Sonnet-4-6) show 13.7%/14.4% performance declines on MCP servers evolved by 11 mutation operators (tool, parameter, description level). Drop 'interface-level, backward-compatible'; metric is LLM-judged Task Fulfillment (1-10), Sec 6.2 'Main Results'.

evidence: arXiv:2609.37864 (Yiming Cheng + 10 others, 29 Sep 2026). Abstract contains the quoted phrase and Live-Harness-Bench with 200 reproducible harness bugs, but does not say bugs are mined from issues; says discovered from open-source agentic systems.
correction: Real harness bugs in open-source agentic systems can be automatically discovered and reproduced as executable instances (Live-Harness-Bench, 200 bugs); 10.67-27.56% higher reproduction success than general bug-reproduction techniques. Remove 'from issues' unless confirmed in body [verify].

evidence: arXiv:2608.06790 (Tan ... Lo; ASE 2026). Injection targets LLM API responses (e.g. /chat/completions); 'Requests to other URLs pass through unchanged.' 'pass@1 dropping by up to 50 percentage points' is aggregate across all 65 fault configs, not value faults.
correction: Fault injection (crash/omission/value) on LLM API responses at the HTTP layer degrades agent systems by up to 50 pp pass@1 (across all fault types); existing diagnosis methods <53% accuracy on fault type, <56% on fault step. It injects into model-provider responses, not tool results.
